### ITHC-001 — Hardcoded Database Password in appSettings

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Severity** | 🔴 Critical |
| **CVSSv3 Score** | 9.8 |
| **CVSSv3 Vector** | `AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` |
| **CWE** | CWE-798 – Use of Hard-coded Credentials |
| **OWASP** | A07:2021 – Identification and Authentication Failures |
| **Affected File** | `Web.config` |
| **Line** | 38 |
| **Function/Class** | Application Configuration |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Remediation Deadline** | 24 hours |
| **Retested** | No |
| **Source Tool** | Secrets Scan |
| **AI Confidence** | N/A |

**Description:**  
The database connection string stored in `appSettings` contains a plaintext password (`Password=password`). Any developer, operator, or attacker with read access to `Web.config` (including via a path traversal or LFI vulnerability) obtains full credentials to the BSE SQL Server database.

**Evidence (redacted):**
```xml
<add key="DBConnectionString"
	 value="Data Source=vm-aphadev-003;Initial Catalog=BSE;
			User Id=BSESystemUser;Password=[REDACTED: DB_PASSWORD];" />
```

**Impact:**  
Complete compromise of the BSE database — full read/write/delete access to all case data, audit logs, and personally identifiable information.

**Recommendation:**
1. Remove the connection string from `Web.config` immediately.
2. Store credentials in Azure Key Vault or use Windows Integrated Authentication (no username/password required).
3. Rotate the `BSESystemUser` database password on target server `vm-aphadev-003`.
4. Use `<connectionStrings>` with `configSource` pointing to a file excluded from source control, or inject via environment variables.

**References:**  
[CWE-798](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/798.html) | [NCSC: Password management](https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/collection/passwords)

### ITHC-002 — SQL Server SA Credentials in sessionState Configuration

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Severity** | 🔴 Critical |
| **CVSSv3 Score** | 9.1 |
| **CVSSv3 Vector** | `AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:L` |
| **CWE** | CWE-798 – Use of Hard-coded Credentials |
| **OWASP** | A07:2021 – Identification and Authentication Failures |
| **Affected File** | `Web.config` |
| **Line** | 113 |
| **Function/Class** | Application Configuration (`sessionState`) |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Remediation Deadline** | 24 hours |
| **Retested** | No |
| **Source Tool** | Secrets Scan |
| **AI Confidence** | N/A |

**Description:**  
The `sessionState` element contains a `sqlConnectionString` referencing `user id=sa` with an empty password. The SA (System Administrator) account is the highest-privileged SQL Server account. An empty password means the SA account requires no authentication on this SQL Server instance.

**Evidence (redacted):**
```xml
<sessionState mode="InProc"
  sqlConnectionString="data source=127.0.0.1;user id=sa;password=[REDACTED: EMPTY]"
  cookieless="false" timeout="20" />
```

**Impact:**  
Full sysadmin access to the SQL Server instance at `127.0.0.1`. An attacker able to reach this server (e.g., through SSRF, server-side access, or compromised app host) can exfiltrate all databases, execute OS commands via `xp_cmdshell`, and achieve system-level compromise.

**Recommendation:**
1. Disable the `sa` account on the SQL Server instance: `ALTER LOGIN sa DISABLE;`
2. Assign a strong password to `sa` even if disabled, as defence in depth.
3. Session state should use `InProc` (already configured) or Windows-authenticated SQL session state — remove the `sqlConnectionString` element entirely.
4. Enable SQL Server mixed-mode authentication audit logging.

**References:**  
[CWE-798](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/798.html) | [MSSQL: Disable SA](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/relational-databases/security/choose-an-authentication-mode)

### ITHC-003 — ASP.NET Compilation debug="true" in Production Configuration

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Severity** | 🟠 High |
| **CVSSv3 Score** | 7.5 |
| **CVSSv3 Vector** | `AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N` |
| **CWE** | CWE-215 – Insertion of Sensitive Information into Debugging Code |
| **OWASP** | A05:2021 – Security Misconfiguration |
| **Affected File** | `Web.config` |
| **Line** | 70 |
| **Function/Class** | `<compilation>` |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Remediation Deadline** | 7 days |
| **Retested** | No |
| **Source Tool** | SAST |
| **AI Confidence** | N/A |

**Description:**  
`debug="true"` is set in the `<compilation>` element. This causes ASP.NET to emit detailed stack traces, SQL queries, and internal state information in error responses. It also disables script optimization and request timeout limits.

**Evidence:**
```xml
<compilation defaultLanguage="vb" debug="true">
```

**Impact:**  
Attackers receive full .NET stack traces in error responses, revealing internal class names, file paths, SQL schema, and business logic — directly aiding exploitation of other vulnerabilities.

**Recommendation:**
1. Set `debug="false"` in `Web.config` for all non-development deployments.
2. Use `<deployment retail="true" />` in `machine.config` as a safety override that ignores per-app debug settings.
3. Enforce via CI/CD pipeline: fail build if `debug="true"` detected in release config transform.

**References:**  
[CWE-215](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/215.html) | [ASP.NET deployment config](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/web-forms/overview/deployment/)

### ITHC-004 — customErrors Disabled (Full Error Details Exposed to Users)

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Severity** | 🟠 High |
| **CVSSv3 Score** | 7.5 |
| **CVSSv3 Vector** | `AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N` |
| **CWE** | CWE-209 – Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information |
| **OWASP** | A05:2021 – Security Misconfiguration |
| **Affected File** | `Web.config` |
| **Line** | 79 |
| **Function/Class** | `<customErrors>` |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Remediation Deadline** | 7 days |
| **Retested** | No |
| **Source Tool** | SAST |
| **AI Confidence** | N/A |

**Description:**  
`customErrors mode="Off"` disables ASP.NET's custom error pages and causes full unhandled exception details — including stack traces, file paths, and connection strings — to be rendered directly in the browser for all users.

**Evidence:**
```xml
<customErrors mode="Off" />
```

**Impact:**  
Any unhandled exception exposes complete diagnostic information to any user or attacker, including internal server paths, database schema, and application structure.

**Recommendation:**
1. Change to `<customErrors mode="On" defaultRedirect="~/GenericError.aspx" />` for production.
2. Use `mode="RemoteOnly"` during development (shows details only on localhost).
3. Implement a generic `GenericError.aspx` with a safe, user-friendly message.

**References:**  
[CWE-209](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/209.html) | [OWASP Error Handling](https://owasp.org/www-community/Improper_Error_Handling)

### ITHC-005 — Exception Message and Stack Trace Rendered to UI

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Severity** | 🟠 High |
| **CVSSv3 Score** | 7.5 |
| **CVSSv3 Vector** | `AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N` |
| **CWE** | CWE-209 – Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information |
| **OWASP** | A05:2021 – Security Misconfiguration |
| **Affected Files** | `AppError.aspx.vb` (L36–38), `SearchCase.aspx.vb` (L213), `SearchCaseByHerdmark.aspx.vb` (L82), `SearchCPHH.aspx.vb` (L94), `SearchFarm.aspx.vb` (L139), `SearchOutstandingData.aspx.vb` (L120), `SearchRelatedAnimal.aspx.vb` (L123), `VLAHeader.ascx.vb` (L100–102) |
| **Line** | Multiple (see above) |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Remediation Deadline** | 7 days |
| **Retested** | No |
| **Source Tool** | SAST |
| **AI Confidence** | N/A |

**Description:**  
Multiple ASPX pages and user controls assign `ex.Message`, `ex.Source`, and `ex.StackTrace` directly to visible UI labels. This is a code-level complement to ITHC-004: even with `customErrors` enabled, these pages would still leak exception details.

**Evidence:**
```vb
' AppError.aspx.vb — lines 36–38 (worst case: full stack trace in browser)
lblAdditional.Text = ex.Message & "<br>Source: " _
				   & ex.Source & "<br>Stack trace:" _
				   & "<br>" & ex.StackTrace

' SearchCase.aspx.vb — line 213
lblResultError.Text = ex.Message

' VLAHeader.ascx.vb — lines 100–102
sMsg &= vbNewLine & ex.Source
sMsg &= vbNewLine & ex.StackTrace
```

**Impact:**  
SQL error messages reveal table names, column names, stored procedure names, and data types. .NET stack traces reveal internal class hierarchy and file paths. This dramatically reduces attacker effort for SQL injection and other attacks.

**Recommendation:**
1. Replace all `ex.Message`/`ex.StackTrace` UI assignments with a generic message: `"An error occurred. Please contact support."`
2. Log the full exception server-side using `clsAppError.LogMessage(ex)` (already used in codebase).
3. Assign a correlation/reference ID to each error and display only the ID to users.

**References:**  
[CWE-209](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/209.html) | [OWASP: Improper Error Handling](https://owasp.org/www-community/Improper_Error_Handling)

### ITHC-006 — Open Redirect via Unvalidated QueryString (Redirect.aspx)

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Severity** | 🟠 High |
| **CVSSv3 Score** | 7.4 |
| **CVSSv3 Vector** | `AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:L/A:N` |
| **CWE** | CWE-601 – URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect') |
| **OWASP** | A03:2021 – Injection |
| **Affected File** | `Redirect.aspx.vb` |
| **Line** | 22 |
| **Function/Class** | `Page_Load` |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Remediation Deadline** | 7 days |
| **Retested** | No |
| **Source Tool** | SAST |
| **AI Confidence** | N/A |

**Description:**  
`Redirect.aspx` performs an unconditional redirect to the URL provided in the `page` query parameter with no origin validation. An attacker can craft a link such as `/Redirect.aspx?page=https://evil.com/phish` and the application will redirect the user.

**Evidence:**
```vb
' Redirect.aspx.vb — line 22
Response.Redirect(Request.QueryString.Get("page"))
```

**Impact:**  
Enables phishing attacks using the trusted BSE/DEFRA domain name. Users who click a legitimate-looking government URL are silently redirected to an attacker-controlled site. Can be used to steal credentials, session tokens, or deliver malware.

**Recommendation:**
1. Validate the redirect target against an allowlist of permitted internal paths:
   ```vb
   Dim sPage As String = Request.QueryString.Get("page")
   Dim allowedPaths As String() = {"home.aspx", "SearchCase.aspx", "CaseEntryFarm.aspx"}
   If allowedPaths.Contains(sPage.ToLower()) Then
	   Response.Redirect(sPage)
   Else
	   Response.Redirect("home.aspx")
   End If
   ```
2. Alternatively, remove `Redirect.aspx` if it is not required — redirect callers directly.

**References:**  
[CWE-601](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/601.html) | [OWASP: Unvalidated Redirects](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Unvalidated_Redirects_and_Forwards_Cheat_Sheet.html)

### ITHC-008 — Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via Unencoded QueryString in MaintenanceConfirmation.aspx

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Severity** | 🟠 High |
| **CVSSv3 Score** | 8.2 |
| **CVSSv3 Vector** | `AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:L/A:N` |
| **CWE** | CWE-79 – Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (XSS) |
| **OWASP** | A03:2021 – Injection |
| **Affected File** | `MaintenanceConfirmation.aspx.vb` |
| **Line** | 26–27 |
| **Function/Class** | `Page_Load` |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Remediation Deadline** | 7 days |
| **Retested** | No |
| **Source Tool** | SAST |
| **AI Confidence** | N/A |

**Description:**  
The `title` and `message` QueryString parameters are assigned directly to `VLAHeader1.PageTitle` and `lblMessage.Text` without HTML encoding. An attacker can inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript by crafting a URL with a malicious `message` parameter. Several other pages redirect to this page passing data via QueryString (e.g., `ADNSExportGB.aspx.vb` line 151), creating a reflected XSS attack chain.

**Evidence:**
```vb
' MaintenanceConfirmation.aspx.vb — lines 26–27
VLAHeader1.PageTitle = Request.QueryString.Get("title")
lblMessage.Text = Request.QueryString.Get("message")
```
Attack URL example:
```
/MaintenanceConfirmation.aspx?title=Alert&message=<script>document.cookie</script>
```

**Impact:**  
Attacker can steal session cookies, perform actions on behalf of the victim, redirect to phishing pages, or exfiltrate sensitive data displayed on the page — all without any user interaction beyond clicking a link.

**Recommendation:**
1. HTML-encode all QueryString values before rendering:
   ```vb
   lblMessage.Text = Server.HtmlEncode(Request.QueryString.Get("message"))
   VLAHeader1.PageTitle = Server.HtmlEncode(Request.QueryString.Get("title"))
   ```
2. Use `<%: %>` syntax in ASPX markup rather than `<%= %>` for automatic encoding.
3. Consider passing confirmation messages via session rather than QueryString to prevent URL-based injection entirely.

**References:**  
[CWE-79](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/79.html) | [OWASP XSS Prevention Cheat Sheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Cross_Site_Scripting_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html)

### ITHC-009 — Missing HTTP Security Headers (No X-Frame-Options, CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type)

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Severity** | 🟡 Medium |
| **CVSSv3 Score** | 6.1 |
| **CVSSv3 Vector** | `AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:N` |
| **CWE** | CWE-693 – Protection Mechanism Failure |
| **OWASP** | A05:2021 – Security Misconfiguration |
| **Affected File** | `Web.config` |
| **Line** | N/A (headers absent) |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Remediation Deadline** | 30 days |
| **Retested** | No |
| **Source Tool** | SAST |
| **AI Confidence** | N/A |

**Description:**  
No HTTP security response headers are configured in `Web.config`. The application does not send `X-Frame-Options`, `Content-Security-Policy`, `Strict-Transport-Security`, or `X-Content-Type-Options`. This leaves the application vulnerable to clickjacking, MIME sniffing attacks, and protocol downgrade.

**Recommendation:**
Add the following to `Web.config` under `<system.webServer>`:
```xml
<httpProtocol>
  <customHeaders>
	<add name="X-Frame-Options" value="SAMEORIGIN" />
	<add name="X-Content-Type-Options" value="nosniff" />
	<add name="X-XSS-Protection" value="1; mode=block" />
	<add name="Strict-Transport-Security" value="max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains" />
	<add name="Content-Security-Policy" value="default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline';" />
  </customHeaders>
</httpProtocol>
```

**References:**  
[OWASP Security Headers](https://owasp.org/www-project-secure-headers/) | [NCSC TLS guidance](https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/guidance/tls-external-facing-services)

### ITHC-010 — No CSRF Protection on Web Forms (86 Postback Pages)

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Severity** | 🟡 Medium |
| **CVSSv3 Score** | 6.5 |
| **CVSSv3 Vector** | `AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N` |
| **CWE** | CWE-352 – Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) |
| **OWASP** | A01:2021 – Broken Access Control |
| **Affected Files** | All 86 ASPX forms with `runat="server"` postbacks |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Remediation Deadline** | 30 days |
| **Retested** | No |
| **Source Tool** | SAST |
| **AI Confidence** | N/A |

**Description:**  
No CSRF tokens or ViewState MAC enforcement were found across the 86 ASP.NET Web Forms pages. ASP.NET Web Forms provides some inherent CSRF protection via ViewState if `EnableViewStateMac="true"` (the default), but this has not been explicitly enforced and no anti-CSRF tokens are used in any form.

**Recommendation:**
1. Ensure `EnableViewStateMac="true"` in all pages (this is the ASP.NET default, but should be confirmed).
2. Set a strong `machineKey` in `Web.config` with `validationKey` and `decryptionKey` using `IsolateApps`.
3. For sensitive operations (case save, delete), add an explicit CSRF token check using a custom `HttpModule` or the `AntiForgery` pattern.

**References:**  
[CWE-352](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/352.html) | [OWASP CSRF Prevention](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Cross-Site_Request_Forgery_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html)

### ITHC-012 — Hardcoded Role Names for Authorization Logic

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Severity** | 🟡 Medium |
| **CVSSv3 Score** | 5.0 |
| **CVSSv3 Vector** | `AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:H/A:N` |
| **CWE** | CWE-284 – Improper Access Control |
| **OWASP** | A01:2021 – Broken Access Control |
| **Affected Files** | Multiple `.vb` files containing `sGroupName = "DEFRA Viewer"`, `"DEFRA Data Entry"`, `"VLA Maintenance"`, etc. |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Remediation Deadline** | 30 days |
| **Retested** | No |
| **Source Tool** | AI-Assisted |
| **AI Confidence** | 0.78 |

**Description:**  
Authorization decisions throughout the codebase use hardcoded string comparisons against role names (e.g., `If sGroupName = "DEFRA Viewer" Then`). This pattern is brittle — any rename of an AD group breaks authorization silently. Crucially, if the group name check fails to match due to a typo or AD group change, users may be granted no permissions or, depending on the fallback logic, more permissions than intended.

**Evidence:**
```vb
If sGroupName = "DEFRA Viewer" Then
	...
ElseIf sGroupName = "DEFRA Data Entry" Then
	...
ElseIf sGroupName = "VLA Maintenance" Then
	...
End If
```

**Recommendation:**
1. Extract group name constants to a shared `SecurityConstants.vb` module.
2. Centralise role-to-permission mapping to a single location (e.g., `clsAuthorisation`).
3. During Entra ID migration, map legacy AD group names to Entra ID app roles and validate against those.

**Description:**  
`ExcelExport.aspx` serves a DataTable stored in session (`SV_ExcelExport`) as a downloadable Excel file. There is no explicit access control check on this page — any authenticated user who can reach the URL may be able to trigger an export. If session variables can be manipulated (e.g., via session fixation or CSRF), arbitrary data could be exported.

**Evidence:**

Dim objDatatable As DataTable = Session.Item(SessionVars.SV_ExcelExport)
...
Response.ContentType = "application/vnd.ms-excel"

The `net20` target framework mismatch may indicate this dependency is no longer actively resolved.

**Recommendation:**
1. Upgrade `AjaxControlToolkit` to the latest stable release compatible with .NET Framework 4.x.
2. Remove if not actively used — search codebase for `AjaxControlToolkit` usage.
3. Update `targetFramework` to `net48` to match the project target.

### ITHC-015 — HTML Injection via Server-Side Error Strings in InnerHtml

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Severity** | 🟡 Medium |
| **CVSSv3 Score** | 4.3 |
| **CVSSv3 Vector** | `AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N` |
| **CWE** | CWE-79 – Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation |
| **OWASP** | A03:2021 – Injection |
| **Affected File** | `CaseEntrySave.aspx.vb` |
| **Line** | 48, 58, 62 |
| **Function/Class** | `PerformSave` |
| **Status** | Open |
| **Remediation Deadline** | 30 days |
| **Retested** | No |
| **Source Tool** | SAST |
| **AI Confidence** | N/A |

**Description:**  
`ctlDIV.InnerHtml` is assigned using `Join(objErrorlist.ToArray, ...)`. The `objErrorlist` is populated by `objCase.CheckMandatoryFields` and `objCase.UpdateCaseDetails` — server-side library methods. While not directly from user input, error messages from the BSELib library may include field values or data that was originally derived from user input, creating a second-order HTML injection risk.

**Evidence:**
```vb
ctlDIV.InnerHtml = "<p>The case is missing the following items of data:</p>" & _
				   Join(objErrorlist.ToArray, "</p><p>") & "</p>"
```

**Recommendation:**
1. HTML-encode each message in `objErrorlist` before joining:
   ```vb
   Dim encodedErrors = objErrorlist.ToArray().Select(Function(m) Server.HtmlEncode(CStr(m)))
   ctlDIV.InnerHtml = "<p>" & String.Join("</p><p>", encodedErrors) & "</p>"
   ```
2. Ensure BSELib does not include raw user input in error message strings.
